title: Judge Navi Pillay Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
summary:
Navi Pillay, a judge and human rights lawyer from South Africa, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. It was announced on Friday.

The Nobel Committee called her a "legal pioneer" with great courage. It said it chose her at a time when "institutions of international law are under political attack." International law is the set of rules countries agree to follow.

Pillay grew up in South Africa under apartheid, a system that treated people unfairly because of their race. She faced unfair treatment but rose to the top of the legal world.

She is now a judge on the International Court of Justice, a United Nations court. She once led the UN's human rights office. She was also a judge at the International Criminal Court and at a court for crimes from the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.

Stephen Rapp, a former US official, said her work always respected victims and survivors.

Hours after the prize was announced, the US government put sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
why_it_matters: Pillay's story shows that someone who was treated unfairly as a child can grow up to help protect the rights of people around the world.
